articles.title: The ‘Gen Z stare’ — and the decline of saying things out loud
articles.summary: It’s become a familiar TikTok trope. A millennial walks into a coffee shop and tries to order something. There are countless iterations, but the basic dynami...
articles.body:
A millennial walks into a coffee shop and tries to order something. There are countless iterations, but the basic dynamic is the same: The cashier responds with a gawp, says as little as possible and points to a sign. Another question; another point. One more question. Point. Eye roll.

Like most good generational jokes, poking fun at the now-infamous "Gen Z stare" - a silent, blank expression - works because it gets at something real: We are, quite literally, talking less.

An analysis published in July in Perspectives on Psychological Science of more than 2,000 people found that Americans and people in several other countries are speaking roughly 300 fewer words a day, or about two to three minutes' worth, with each passing year. The drop - a 28 percent decline from 2005 to 2019 - was especially pronounced among people younger than 25.

The finding raises an obvious question about the influence of smartphones, texting, remote work and other technologies that have allowed us to conduct more of daily life without opening our mouths.

Valeria Pfeifer, the study's lead author and an assistant professor of psychology and counseling at the University of Missouri at Kansas City, came to the finding by accident. She was studying gender differences in speech when she noticed something unexpected in the data: People seemed to be talking less. Curious, she went back to see whether the pattern held - and how much had changed. Only when she looked across the full 14-year span did the scale of the lost words become apparent.

"Once that insight came, it was a big and alarming observation," Pfeifer said.

For most of human history, speaking was not merely one way to communicate. It was the default. You could write a letter, perhaps. But buying something, finding your way around, meeting a stranger, working alongside someone or maintaining a friendship generally required oral conversation.

Now speech is becoming, in many corners of life, optional.

Scientists have long treated changes in speech as a window into the brain. Language difficulties are common in dementia and other neurological disorders. Some patients struggle to retrieve words or express themselves; others have trouble understanding what is said to them. This relationship is usually understood in one direction: The brain changes, and speech changes with it.

But the causal arrow may be messier than that.

Speaking is itself a complicated neurological act.

Producing even an ordinary sentence requires the brain to retrieve words, organize them, coordinate muscles, interpret another person's response and formulate what comes next - all in a fraction of a second. Regions in our brains, including Broca's area in the left hemisphere, play important roles in speech production and articulation.

That raises a provocative possibility. If conversation repeatedly recruits these systems, could talking itself function as a modest form of cognitive exercise? And if so, what happens when people do less of it?

The question is difficult to separate from another change in American life. We are not simply talking less; in many ways, we are spending less time together. Decades of research have linked social connection and cognitive stimulation to better health, while isolation has been associated with worse outcomes.

None of this means that ordering from a touch screen will give someone dementia. But a society-wide decline in ordinary conversation could be one piece of a much larger transformation in how often we exercise our brains by interacting with other people.

Robert Putnam, the Harvard political scientist whose 2000 book "Bowling Alone" chronicled the collapse of American civic participation, sees the decline in spoken interaction as part of a long-standing, broader retreat from face-to-face life. Americans began withdrawing from clubs, churches, neighborhood organizations and other forms of communal participation in the 1960s shortly after TV took off but decades before smartphones arrived. Digital life may be accelerating a process already well underway.

"In some sense, that's the most disturbing thing - that it's still declining," Putnam told me. "It seems impossible to turn that trend around."

For years, the consequences of that retreat have mostly been discussed in social terms: loneliness, polarization, fraying communities, fewer friendships. But if conversation is not simply a means of transmitting information - if it is also a demanding cognitive activity - then its disappearance raises a different set of questions.

Calvin Newport, a Georgetown University professor who writes about the impact of tech on society, said he believes people are talking less because in-person or voice interactions can be hard. But that's the point of it, he said.

"The problem is that our social brains equate sacrificing time and attention on behalf of someone else as the key sign of an important connection. So, when we make socializing easier, we paradoxically feel less connected and social," Newport said.

Gen Z appears to have been especially affected, prompting speculation that the pandemic may be partly to blame: Many young people missed critical years of in-person socialization while attending school virtually during covid-19 lockdowns. On social media, interpretations of the Gen Z stare vary. Some see it as rude, or as evidence of an aversion to small talk. Others describe it more sympathetically, as a deer-in-the-headlights response from young people who feel anxious or unsure of how to respond.

The strange thing about the decline of conversation is that almost no individual instance of it feels like a loss. The kiosk is faster. The app is easier. The text is less awkward. Each innovation saves us a few words.

Only in aggregate do we begin to wonder what all those unsaid words were doing for us.

Pfeifer's study drew on audio recordings from 22 different studies, in which participants carried devices for several days as they went about their daily lives.

In the months since making the discovery, Pfeifer has found herself thinking more about how often she talks - and about what might be lost when conversation is replaced by text. What interests her most is the difference between communicating asynchronously and talking to someone in real time.

A live conversation places particular demands on working memory and attention. You have to keep track of what another person has said, decide how to respond and listen as you formulate what comes next. Texting and email relieve some of that pressure. A message can be considered, revised and re-revised before it is sent; the conversation itself remains on the screen, eliminating much of the need to remember what came before.

Pfeifer suspects that any decline in speech may have less to do with conversations among close friends and family than with the disappearance of smaller, more incidental exchanges mostly with strangers. A burger can be ordered from a kiosk. Google can give directions. ChatGPT can help settle debates about facts such as who was the actor in a certain movie. Each innovation eliminates an interaction that once might have required talking to another person.

"I grew up where, if you are walking the street and a stranger comes towards you, you have to greet them," said Pfeifer, who is now 37 and from a rural area in northern Germany. "I feel like norms are starting to shift towards the polite thing is not to talk to somebody."

Yet research suggests that talking to strangers - even when it feels awkward - tends to make people happier and more connected than they expect, and spoken conversation creates a stronger sense of connection than texting.

Lately, she has been trying to counter her own loss of words. On a recent trip to the airport in Charlotte, on her way home from a work trip, Pfeifer remarked to her driver that it was a beautiful morning. The comment turned into a conversation about where she was headed and about the driver's cousin, who was starting school in St. Louis. On the plane, a comment about the blanket her seatmate brought aboard led her to learn that her seatmate was taking her first flight. Even an exchange at Starbucks at home in Kansas City about whether a drink should be hot or cold became a conversation about the different defaults people expect in different places.

None of these conversations were especially consequential. But the small exchanges provided opportunities to exercise the social and cognitive skills that connecting with another human requires.

"I think these small acts can go a long way to develop more confidence in talking with each other again," Pfeifer said.

articles.title: What Is ‘Lore-Tripping’? The Quirky Travel Trend We Can’t Wait To Try This Fall
articles.summary: “Lore-tripping” is having a moment this fall. Discover the Southern small towns and quirky destinations Airbnb says Gen Z travelers are seeking out.
articles.body:
I consider myself to be pretty well-traveled. This year, I've crossed a new continent off my list and even hiked my first volcano. So people are often surprised when I tell them my might have been to Louisville, Kentucky. Or that I'm a Southerner with a special place in her heart for Madison, Wisconsin.

After years of gallivanting around the globe, I've learned some of the best travel memories can be waiting in the most unexpected places. And I'm not the only one who feels this way. Airbnb's latest travel trends note that Gen Z travelers are trading in "Instagrammable" destinations for lesser-known towns this fall. Visiting quirky places might be nothing new, but if you need a reminder to take the road less traveled, "lore-tripping" might just be the trend to take a cue from this fall.

Lore-tripping is all about prioritizing over major cities and traditional hotspots. This fall, Gen Z is taking more "lore-trips," setting its sights on under-the-radar, quirky towns with "colorful backstories." According to Airbnb, nearly half of Gen Z's trending fall destinations are small towns.

So, what's driving this affection for smaller towns? For many travelers, it comes down to getting more for their money, experiencing a place on a more local, authentic level, and finding unusual attractions they won't see anywhere else. And Gen Z's interest in small-town travel is showing up in the numbers, too. Airbnb searches for southern destinations like Hot Springs, Arkansas, are up 30 percent among the generation, while searches for Helen, Georgia, are up 15 percent. The only question now is: Where in the South should you "lore-trip" this fall?

Small Towns In The South Worth Visiting This Fall

We're big fans of tiny towns and . Here are the Southern spots that made Airbnb's list.

Hot Springs, AR : In the Ouachita Mountains, Hot Springs is home to 47 natural springs and the historic bathhouses of . After soaking up the town's spa-town history, explore Garvan Woodland Gardens or head out to one of the area's three major lakes for a day on the water.

Helen, GA : You don't have to cross the Atlantic to get a taste of Bavaria. This tiny mountain town has German-inspired architecture, cobblestone streets, and plenty of outdoor adventures. And if you visit in the fall, you may just catch Helen's famous Oktoberfest festivities, which kick off in September.

Point Pleasant, WV: If your idea of a memorable getaway involves a little mystery, Point Pleasant has you covered. The Ohio River town is best known as the birthplace of the Mothman legend, which dates back to a series of reported sightings in 1966. Visit the Mothman statue and museum downtown, then explore the TNT area where the mysterious creature was reportedly spotted.

Gibsonton, FL : Just south of Tampa, this quirky community—better known as "Gibtown"—has an unusual claim to fame: it was once a winter haven for circus and carnival performers. Today, its sideshow history is still part of what makes Gibtown unlike anywhere else.

articles.title: Third Burning Man festivalgoer dies, officials say
articles.summary: Craigh Mann, 60, was found dead in his camp in Black Rock City, Nevada, on Saturday, the festival said. No cause of death was disclosed.
articles.body:
A Burning Man attendee died while being taken to a hospital, officials said Monday, the third reported death of a festivalgoer in less than a week.

The person was en route to a hospital in Reno, roughly 120 miles south of Black Rock City, Nevada, where the festival takes place, when they died, the Pershing County Sheriff's Office said.

"Although we average 1 death a year at the Festival, we have had two so far this year within the confines of the Festival and I have received information regarding a third who died in transit to a hospital in Reno," Jerry Allen, Pershing County sheriff and coroner, said in a statement Monday.

Allen said the death occurred in Washoe County jurisdiction. The Washoe County Sheriff's Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The festival said Saturday that a second attendee, Craig Mann, 60, was found dead in his camp in Black Rock City at 3 p.m. No cause of death was disclosed.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the participant's family, friends, campmates, and all those affected by this loss," the festival said in a statement.

When deputies responded, Mann was found dead in his trailer, which he was sharing with his partner, Allen said in a news release Monday.

A preliminary investigation did not indicate signs of foul play, Allen said.

It was the second death reported at the annual psychedelic, music and art festival in the Nevada desert, which draws a crowd of about 70,000.

The festival said last week that a man in his mid-50s died after a medical emergency.

Deputies found Sampson Tshombe dead after responding to the temporary hospital located at the festival on Thursday, Allen said.

He "immediately received lifesaving measures, and was transported to the onsite center for emergency care where he was pronounced deceased," the festival said.

Allen said the sheriff's office's investigation revealed Tshombe had "been found on a street within the Festival and emergency personnel had performed CPR on him for several minutes, until a certified doctor pronounced Sampson deceased."

As with Mann, officials ruled out signs of foul play in the Tshombe's death.

The Washoe County Medical Examiner's Office will conduct autopsies and toxicology screenings for both festivalgoers, with results expected in six to eight weeks, Allen said.

The festival started Aug. 30 and is scheduled through Monday.

articles.title: Marconi Perillo promete metrô e subsídio no transporte do Entorno | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSDB participou de culto em Formosa e detalhou propostas para a região. Entre as principais promessas estão o subsídio nas passagens de ônibus, metronização e melhorias na saúde pública.
articles.summary: Marconi Perillo detalha planos para subsidiar passagens de ônibus, implementar o metrô e zerar filas da saúde em Formosa e cidades do Entorno de Goiás.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo de Goiás, Marconi Perillo ( PSDB ), participou nesta segunda-feira (7) de um culto em uma igreja evangélica de Formosa , no Entorno do Distrito Federal. Marconi foi recebido por lideranças religiosas, cumprimentou fiéis e apresentou propostas para famílias atípicas. Entre as prioridades está o investimento no transporte para as pessoas que vivem em Goiás e trabalham no Distrito Federal, disse o candidato.

Durante a agenda, o candidato afirmou que pretende investir no transporte do Entorno com subsídio nas passagens e metronização. Marconi disse também que, se for eleito, vai ampliar a rede de apoio para pessoas com deficiência. Outra promessa do candidato é zerar as filas de espera para exames e cirurgias e fechar parcerias com hospitais particulares para atender à demanda do sistema público de saúde.

"O que vai resolver o transporte aqui é metrô, é metrô ou BRT. O governo do Estado, desde a minha época, já subsidiava o transporte na região metropolitana de Goiânia. Nós vamos pagar uma parte da passagem para ela ficar mais barata para o usuário", disse Marconi.

Marconi disse ainda que pretende exigir das empresas que elas substituam os ônibus velhos por veículos novos, confortáveis, com ar-condicionado e também com acessibilidade para pessoas com deficiência.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: saiba como foi o dia do candidato Felipe Camarão ao governo do Maranhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato se reuniu com coordenadores de campanha e propôs recuperar a malha viária e descentralizar obras no estado.
articles.summary: Candidato se reuniu com coordenadores de campanha e propôs recuperar a malha viária e descentralizar obras no estado.
articles.body:
Os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão Roberto Rocha (PRTB), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Felipe Camarão (PT) e Saulo Arcângeli (PSTU) cumpriram agenda de campanha nesta segunda-feira (7), em São Luís. Entre os compromissos, eles apresentaram propostas para infraestrutura e obras públicas no estado.

A TV Mirante acompanhou os compromissos dos candidatos e registrou as principais propostas apresentadas por cada um ao longo do dia.

Veja, abaixo, como foi o dia do candidato Felipe Camarão:

Felipe Camarão (PT) — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Mirante

Felipe Camarão (PT) participou de uma reunião com coordenadores de diferentes áreas da campanha no comitê do partido, no bairro do Turu, em São Luís.

Durante o encontro, o candidato apresentou propostas para diferentes áreas da administração pública. Na infraestrutura, afirmou que pretende recuperar a malha viária do estado e descentralizar a execução de obras.

“A nossa primeira medida vai ser o plano de recuperação total da malha viária do nosso Estado, ou seja, todas as estradas, todas as MAs. Com isso, nós vamos garantir apoio logístico, que o Maranhão tanto precisa, que o Maranhão tanto tem a oferecer, juntamente com o nosso porto e nossas condições naturais”, afirmou.

Camarão também disse que pretende dar transparência às obras paradas ou inacabadas e concluir projetos nas áreas de saúde e educação.

“Também vamos dar transparência total às obras que estão paradas e inacabadas no atual governo. [...] Então nós vamos descentralizar essas obras [...] e concluir as obras da saúde, das escolas, da educação, dos hospitais”, disse.

articles.title: Desfile de 7 de Setembro reúne multidão no Centro da capital do Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Devido às altas temperaturas, governo transferiu evento para a tarde. Apresentações de alunos, associações filantrópicas, forças estaduais e do Exército marcaram o evento.
articles.summary: Devido às altas temperaturas, governo transferiu evento para a tarde. Apresentações de alunos, associações filantrópicas, forças estaduais e do Exército marcaram o evento.
articles.body:
O desfile cívico-militar de 7 de Setembro reuniu uma multidão no Centro de Rio Branco durante o feriado desta segunda-feira. Ao todo, 12 avenidas, ruas e cruzamentos foram bloqueados e outros oito tiveram controle de fluxo durante a programação que ocorre em frente ao palácio da capital acreana.

Por causa das altas temperaturas registradas no Acre, o governo do estado transferiu o desfile deste ano para o período da tarde, além disso, o evento também ganhou um novo percurso.

Este ano, a concentração foi na Rua Marechal Deodoro e o início ocorreu na Avenida Benjamin Constant, em frente ao palácio, onde foi instalada uma arquibancada. O encerramento foi em frente ao Fórum Barão do Rio Branco.

Apresentações de alunos, associações filantrópicas, forças estaduais e do Exército marcaram o evento — Foto: Walace Gomes/g1

A programação começou às 15h, com a concentração dos participantes. A solenidade começou às 16h50, com execução dos hinos da Independência e do Brasil, e o desfile cívico começou às 17h10 e o encerramento está previsto para as 19h.

Alunos de escolas públicas, associações filantrópicas, forças estaduais e a Banda do Exército brilharam nas apresentações.

Adriana Vitória Pereira, de 24 anos, estuda no Centro de Ensino Especial Dom Bosco e participou pela segunda vez do desfile.

"É muito bom estar aqui no desfile e também confraternizando com os amigos da escola, eu gosto muito. É muito bom participar e nesse ano eu ainda estou aqui representando a governadora, só que na minha versão de cachos. É uma diversão", afirmou.

Já a estudante do Colégio Sebastião Pedrosa, Ester Vieira dos Anjos, de 17 anos, falou do orgulho de estrear no desfile neste ano. Ela contou que já tinha assistido a apresentação em anos anteriores, mas nunca desfilou.

"Estou sentindo muito orgulho, é uma honra participar disso aqui. Fiquei maravilhada pois estamos estudando exatamente sobre a identidade brasileira e ser brasileiro, e através da independência do Brasil que nós podemos nos expressar, sendo quem nós somos. Esse momento foi muito lindo", destacou.

Para a diretora da escola Sebastião Pedrosa, Maria Sandy Guedes, o momento é de alegria visto que na sua gestão, é a primeira vez que a escola participa do desfile. "Estamos com 130 estudantes aqui e é muito importante despertar nos alunos a história do sete de setembro e desse patriotismo, é uma felicidade", declarou.

Foram montadas arquibancadas ao longo da Rua Benjamin Constant para que as pessoas acompanhassem as apresentações.

Um dos espectadores que chegou bem antes do começo da festividade foi o professor Helenilson Pereira da Costa, acompanhado da família. Segundo ele, a idéia de levar os filhos para o desfile é uma forma de contar sobre a história do povo brasileiro.

"Venho todos os anos e quero passar esse legado para os meus filhos, junto com minha esposa. É importante eles saberem desse civismo, para que eles possam crescer entendendo que somos um país, livre democrático e que lutou para estarmos onde estamos aqui. Quero seguir com essa tradição até eles estarem independentes", comentou.

articles.title: Movimentos sociais promovem a 32ª edição do Grito dos Excluídos pelo Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Com o lema 'Na defesa da terra, da paz e da moradia, erguemos a voz: mulheres vivas e soberania', a organização ofereceu um café da manhã para pessoas em situação de rua em São Paulo, em frente à Catedral da Sé.
articles.summary: Com o lema 'Na defesa da terra, da paz e da moradia, erguemos a voz: mulheres vivas e soberania', a organização ofereceu um café da manhã para pessoas em situação de rua em São Paulo, em frente à Catedral da Sé.
articles.body:
Neste 7 de Setembro, movimentos sociais promoveram a 32ª edição do Grito dos Excluídos .

Com o lema " Na defesa da terra, da paz e da moradia, erguemos a voz: mulheres vivas e soberania ", a organização ofereceu um café da manhã para pessoas em situação de rua em São Paulo, em frente à Catedral da Sé. Depois, os participantes saíram em caminhada pela região central.

No Centro do Rio de Janeiro, os manifestantes chamaram atenção para as desigualdades sociais. O ato percorreu a Avenida Presidente Vargas, uma das principais vias da cidade.

articles.title: Alemanha contesta as acusações de genocídio em Gaza na Corte da ONU | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo maior fornecedor de armas a Israel, país é acusado pela Nicarágua de facilitar atos de genocídio em Gaza com apoio militar. Governo alemão pede arquivamento da ação.
articles.summary: Segundo maior fornecedor de armas a Israel, país é acusado pela Nicarágua de facilitar atos de genocídio em Gaza com apoio militar. Governo alemão pede arquivamento da ação.
articles.body:
A Alemanha pediu nesta segunda-feira (7) que a Corte Internacional de Justiça (CIJ), principal tribunal da ONU, arquive um processo que acusa o país de facilitar atos de genocídio na Faixa de Gaza ao fornecer armas e apoio militar a Israel.

A ação foi apresentada pela Nicarágua, que afirma que o governo alemão violou a Convenção sobre o Genocídio e o direito internacional humanitário. A defesa alemã argumenta que o país centro-americano não seguiu os procedimentos necessários antes de levar o caso ao tribunal, em Haia, na Holanda.

Embora o processo seja contra a Alemanha, ele questiona o apoio à ofensiva israelense em Gaza, iniciada em resposta aos ataques do Hamas de 7 de outubro de 2023. Israel não é parte nessa ação e nega cometer genocídio.

Segundo Julia Monar, principal advogada da Alemanha no caso, a Nicarágua não notificou adequadamente o governo alemão e deu menos de um mês para uma resposta antes de iniciar o processo. Espera-se que os países tentem resolver suas divergências antes de recorrer à corte.

“A conduta da Nicarágua indica que ela não estava interessada em ouvir a versão da Alemanha sobre suas alegações, mas simplesmente em trazer a Alemanha perante este tribunal”, afirmou Monar.

Outro advogado da defesa alemã, Antonios Tzanakopoulos, disse que a notificação foi enviada de um endereço de e-mail do Yahoo para uma caixa de entrada geral, sem seguir os canais diplomáticos apropriados.

A Alemanha é uma aliada histórica de Israel e o segundo maior fornecedor de armas ao país, atrás dos Estados Unidos.

Durante a audiência, Monar afirmou que o governo alemão analisa todas as exportações de equipamentos militares de acordo com o direito internacional.

“A Alemanha não autorizou, desde 2024, a exportação de armas de guerra com destino final a Israel que possam ser usadas no conflito em Gaza”, declarou.

Em 2024, a CIJ rejeitou um pedido de emergência da Nicarágua para obrigar a Alemanha a suspender a ajuda militar e de outros tipos a Israel. Na ocasião, porém, os 16 juízes se recusaram a arquivar o processo.

A ação contra a Alemanha é diferente do processo apresentado pela África do Sul contra Israel, em 2023, também na Corte Internacional de Justiça.

Os dois casos apontam violações da Convenção para a Prevenção e a Repressão do Crime de Genocídio, de 1948, elaborada após o Holocausto.

No processo movido pela África do Sul, a corte determinou, em janeiro de 2024, que Israel adotasse medidas para prevenir atos de genocídio em Gaza. Dois meses depois, ordenou ações para melhorar a situação humanitária, incluindo a abertura de mais passagens terrestres para a entrada de alimentos, água, combustível e outros suprimentos.

A África do Sul afirma que Israel ignorou amplamente essas determinações.

Uma equipe de especialistas independentes criada pelo Conselho de Direitos Humanos da ONU e a maior organização profissional de estudiosos de genocídio concluíram que Israel viola a convenção. Essas conclusões, porém, não equivalem a uma decisão judicial sobre o caso.

O julgamento pode levar anos. Em maio, a corte fixou novembro de 2027 como prazo para a África do Sul apresentar suas alegações por escrito. Israel terá até maio de 2029 para responder.

Com isso, as audiências sobre a questão central, se Israel cometeu genocídio em Gaza, provavelmente só ocorrerão a partir do fim de 2029.

Em um processo separado, o Tribunal Penal Internacional (TPI), também sediado em Haia, emitiu mandados de prisão contra o primeiro-ministro de Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu , e o ex-ministro da Defesa Yoav Gallant.

A diferença é que a CIJ julga disputas entre países, enquanto o TPI julga indivíduos.

Netanyahu e Gallant são acusados de crimes contra a humanidade e crimes de guerra, e não de genocídio. Segundo o tribunal, há motivos para acreditar que os dois usaram a fome como método de guerra, restringiram a ajuda humanitária e dirigiram ataques intencionalmente contra civis. As autoridades israelenses negam as acusações.

Em resposta, os Estados Unidos impuseram sanções a funcionários do TPI, incluindo nove dos 18 juízes.

A guerra deixou dezenas de milhares de palestinos mortos e devastou a Faixa de Gaza. Apesar do cessar-fogo mediado pelos Estados Unidos no ano passado, a violência continua.

Segundo o Ministério da Saúde de Gaza, mais de 1.300 palestinos foram mortos por fogo israelense desde o anúncio da trégua. Cinco soldados israelenses também morreram no período.

articles.title: Castramóvel oferece castração gratuita de cães e gatos em Salvador | G1
articles.standfirst: Atendimentos começam nesta sexta-feira (8), no estacionamento da Ferreira Costa, na Avenida Paralela. Vagas serão preenchidas por ordem de chegada.
articles.summary: Atendimentos começam nesta sexta-feira (8), no estacionamento da Ferreira Costa, na Avenida Paralela. Vagas serão preenchidas por ordem de chegada.
articles.body:
Castramóvel inicia atendimentos na Avenida Paralela — Foto: Prefeitura de Salvador

Cães e gatos de tutores moradores de Salvador poderão ser castrados gratuitamente a partir desta terça-feira (8), quando o Castramóvel inicia atendimento no estacionamento da Ferreira Costa, na Avenida Paralela.

Serão distribuídas 40 fichas por dia para gatos, com atendimento às segundas, quartas e sextas-feiras. Já às terças e quintas-feiras, serão disponibilizadas 30 fichas para cães. As vagas serão preenchidas por ordem de chegada, a partir das 8h.

Para ter acesso ao serviço, o tutor precisa possuir cartão do SUS vinculado ao município de Salvador e apresentar RG, CPF e comprovante de residência.

Para realizar o procedimento, o animal deve ter entre seis meses e cinco anos e 11 meses de idade, estar saudável e com a vacinação antirrábica em dia. Caso ele tenha sido vacinado recentemente, é necessário aguardar pelo menos 15 dias antes de realizar o procedimento. Também é exigido jejum de 10 a 12 horas, inclusive de água, devido à anestesia.

A ação é realizada pela Secretaria de Sustentabilidade, Resiliência, Bem-Estar e Proteção Animal (Secis), por meio da Diretoria de Promoção à Saúde e Proteção Animal (Dipa). Somente em agosto, 1.744 animais foram atendidos pelo serviço.

Além de auxiliar no controle da população de cães e gatos, a castração contribui para a prevenção de doenças e reduz o risco de transmissão de zoonoses, ajudando na promoção da saúde pública.

Segundo a diretora da Dipa, Amanda Elem, a definição dos locais de atendimento busca ampliar o alcance da iniciativa. “Estamos escolhendo com cuidado cada região para que o Castramóvel consiga atender toda a população e as demandas reprimidas”, afirmou.

articles.standfirst: Lideranças na Europa se manifestaram nesta segunda-feira (7) sobre a primeira vitória da extrema-direita em uma eleição na Alemanha desde o fim da Segunda Guerra Mundial.
articles.summary: Lideranças na Europa se manifestaram nesta segunda-feira (7) sobre a primeira vitória da extrema-direita em uma eleição na Alemanha desde o fim da Segunda Guerra Mundial.
articles.body:
Lideranças na Europa se manifestaram nesta segunda-feira (7) sobre a primeira vitória da extrema-direita em uma eleição na Alemanha desde o fim da Segunda Guerra Mundial.

O resultado das urnas na Saxônia-Anhalt virou o jogo na política alemã. Em um dos menores estados do país, que fica no território da antiga Alemanha Oriental e tem pouco mais de 2 milhões de habitantes, um partido de extrema direita conquistou quase 44% dos votos. A Alternativa para a Alemanha, AfD, ganhou 39 das 83 cadeiras do parlamento estadual - três a menos do que a maioria absoluta.

“É um mandato muito claro para governar. Este é o melhor resultado alcançado por qualquer partido na Saxônia-Anhalt desde 1990”, afirmou o deputado que foi a cara da AfD nessa eleição.

Chanceler alemão diz que vitória da extrema-direita em eleição estadual acende alerta na Europa — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Mas vencer não significa governar. Os principais partidos alemães se recusam a cooperar com a AfD, que busca apoio para formar uma maioria. O partido defende a deportação de imigrantes e o fim do apoio à Ucrânia.

“Não é simplesmente mais uma vitória para a AfD. Podemos ver uma mudança fundamental no sistema político”, disse o analista político Oliver Lembcke.

A União Democrática Cristã, partido do primeiro-ministro Friedrich Merz , ficou em um distante segundo lugar. Merz afirmou que o resultado envia uma mensagem ao continente europeu e ao mundo.

O primeiro-ministro espanhol, Pedro Sánchez, disse que a ameaça ganha terreno no continente. Na Itália, aliada da Alemanha nazista durante o regime fascista de Benito Mussolini, o resultado expôs uma divisão no governo. O vice-primeiro-ministro Matteo Salvini comemorou. O ministro das Relações Exteriores, Antonio Tajani, chamou a vitória de “péssima notícia”. A primeira-ministra Giorgia Meloni, que já defendeu uma política ultraconservadora, não se manifestou.

articles.body:
As comemorações da Independência movimentaram cidades em todo o país nesta segunda-feira (7). Em Brasília, o desfile na Esplanada dos Ministérios reuniu autoridades e milhares de pessoas.

Em Brasília, a movimentação na Esplanada dos Ministérios começou às 6h. Antes da chegada do presidente Lula , o público gritou pedindo o fim da escala 6x1, proposta apoiada pelo governo e que tramita no Senado.

Às 9h10, Lula percorreu a Esplanada no tradicional Rolls-Royce presidencial. No palanque estavam o vice-presidente, Geraldo Alckmin, os presidentes do STF, ministro Luiz Edson Fachin ; do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre ; da Câmara, Hugo Motta, e ministros do governo.

No domingo (6), o presidente fez um discurso em rede nacional pelo 7 de Setembro, que teve como tema principal a defesa da soberania:

“Defender a independência do Brasil é defender nossa soberania e nossa democracia. Mais do que nunca, é preciso lutar pelo que é nosso. Temos a segunda maior reserva de terras raras do mundo, e a maior fonte de água doce. No último mês, descobrimos uma nova e rica reserva de petróleo. Nossas riquezas devem servir ao futuro do povo brasileiro”.

A cerimônia nesta segunda-feira (7) começou com estudantes. Depois, as Forças Armadas, a Polícia Militar e o Corpo de Bombeiros. O desfile em comemoração aos 204 anos da independência do Brasil destacou três temas: soberania nacional, enfrentamento à violência contra as mulheres e a Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027. Para encerrar, a pirâmide humana do batalhão do Exército. No céu, a Esquadrilha da Fumaça.

Comemorações da Independência movimentam cidades pelo Brasil — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Em São Paulo, com frio e garoa, o desfile no Anhembi teve coral e fanfarras. No Rio, atletas medalhistas acenderam a pira com o fogo simbólico da pátria. Em Belo Horizonte, o público teve que levar capa e guarda-chuva. Destaque para o cachorro-robô da PM.

Em Curitiba, o público enfrentou o frio para ver carros antigos do Exército. Em Porto Alegre, o desfile foi na orla do Guaiba.

No Recife, uma das atrações foi o Guarani, a viatura blindada desenvolvida no Brasil. Em Salvador, o desfile conquistou novos admiradores.

“Eu amo esse show, é a primeira vez que eu vou”, diz o estudante Caique Silva.

articles.title: Calor em Manaus: MIT e UFAM estudam ilhas de calor na cidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados recolhidos serão utilizados como referência para uma ferramenta de avaliação de políticas climáticas. Universidade Federal do Amazonas em parceria com o Instituto de Tecnologia de Massachusetts.
articles.summary: Parceria entre UFAM e MIT analisa ilhas de calor em Manaus para criar ferramentas de planejamento urbano e combater as mudanças climáticas na região.
articles.body:
Representantes do MIT e Ufam se reuniram com o Implurb na sede do órgão para discutir a integração de Manaus em estudo sobre calor urbano. — Foto: Maxwell Oliveira/Implurb

A Universidade Federal do Amazonas ( UFAM ), em parceria com o Instituto de Tecnologia de Massachusetts ( MIT ), estudará as condições térmicas de diferentes áreas em Manaus . A capital amazonense será uma das localidades estudadas em uma pesquisa sobre a influência das características do ambiente urbano na formação de ilhas de calor em cidades tropicais.

Entre os pontos de coleta de dados, está a sede do Instituto Municipal de Planejamento Urbano (Implurb), que também participa do estudo, e um edifício localizado no Parque Mosaico, no bairro Tarumã, zona Oeste de Manaus. Os resultados serão utilizados como referência para a construção de um modelo físico-matemático capaz de avaliar estratégias de redução do calor urbano.

Segundo a pesquisadora Sylvia Jiménez Riofrío, doutoranda do MIT, Manaus foi escolhida por sua importância para o estudo das cidades amazônicas:

“Manaus é a maior cidade amazônica da região, e sua importância não é apenas para o Brasil, mas para toda a América Latina. O que Manaus faz em planejamento urbano impacta não somente as cidades da região, mas todas as cidades amazônicas latino-americanas”, afirmou.

O estudo também deve analisar aspectos como conforto térmico, desempenho das edificações e consumo de energia.

O arquiteto Marcos Cereto, coordenador do Grupo de Pesquisa Arquitetura Moderna na Amazônia (Grupo AMA) da UFAM, que integra a pesquisa, diz que a participação da universidade no estudo contribuirá para o desenvolvimento da capital amazonense:

"O papel da universidade é produzir conhecimento que possa contribuir diretamente para o planejamento urbano. Essa parceria entre a Ufam, o MIT e o Implurb permitirá coletar informações capazes de subsidiar futuras atualizações da legislação urbanística, especialmente em temas relacionados ao conforto térmico, ao desempenho das edificações e ao consumo de energia nas metrópoles”, afirmou

O vice-presidente do Implurb, o arquiteto e urbanista Pedro Paulo Cordeiro, também explicou que os dados serão utilizados em futuros projetos para o planejamento urbano de Manaus:

"Vivemos um período de mudanças climáticas cada vez mais intensas. Esse estudo permitirá identificar como o calor se distribui em diferentes regiões da cidade, fornecendo dados concretos para embasar futuras diretrizes urbanísticas. É um conhecimento científico que poderá orientar soluções mais eficientes para o conforto térmico, o uso do solo e a qualidade dos espaços urbanos”, disse.

articles.title: Assalto em Belém: criminosos fingem ser entregadores na Cremação | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois homens armados usavam mochilas e capacetes de entregadores. Quatro trabalhadores foram rendidos e tiveram celulares e outros pertences roubados no bairro da Cremação.
articles.summary: Assalto em Belém ocorreu na Cremação; dupla armada rendeu quatro trabalhadores e roubou celulares em um ponto de venda de refeições por delivery.
articles.body:
Dois homens armados se passaram por entregadores para assaltar quatro trabalhadores em um ponto de venda de refeições por delivery no bairro da Cremação, em Belém . O crime ocorreu por volta de 13h30 de domingo (6), na travessa 9 de Janeiro, entre as ruas dos Pariquis e dos Mundurucus.

Os dois chegaram ao local usando mochilas e capacetes, como os utilizados por entregadores. Depois de entrarem no imóvel, anunciaram o assalto e renderam quatro homens que trabalham com entregas e aguardavam para pegar encomendas.

Durante a ação, as vítimas foram obrigadas a se deitar no chão. Imagens registraram o momento em que um dos assaltantes dá um tapa em um dos trabalhadores.

Em seguida, os criminosos recolheram celulares e outros pertences das vítimas. Após pegar o último aparelho, a dupla fugiu.

O imóvel onde ocorreu o assalto funciona como ponto de venda de refeições por delivery. Após o crime, as vítimas preferiram não comentar o caso.

articles.title: Take it or leave it: Across Delhi, they put lives on line to study
articles.summary: Delhi PGs in student hubs like Mukherjee Nagar and Laxmi Nagar raise safety fears after Satya Niketan collapse, with cramped lanes, exposed wires and high rents.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In Delhi’s student hubs, finding a PG accommodation can mean squeezing through cramped lanes and narrow staircases in tightly-packed buildings.“PG available” signs compete with tangled wires and exposed meters. In some pockets, dug-up approach roads and poor ventilation add to the worry. Yet, students pay steep rents for small rooms simply to stay close to college and coaching centres.The building collapse in Satya Niketan has renewed concerns over safety in the city’s student and coaching hubs, where many students depend on private accommodation.In areas like Laxmi Nagar and adjoining Shakarpur and West Angad Nagar, PGs and rented rooms have proliferated around coaching centres. Some buildings stand along narrow, uneven or excavated stretches, while overhead cables form a dense web between structures, at places almost obscuring their facades.“We stay here mainly because our coaching classes are close by. The lanes are congested and there are wires hanging everywhere, but what choice do we have? This is what fits my budget. If I look for a better or more spacious place, the rent goes up considerably, and as a student, I simply cannot afford that,” said Anamika, a student living in Shakurpur.In several properties, rooms have been carved out of packed buildings, leaving little room for ventilation or movement. “A double-sharing room starts at Rs 10,000 and can go up to Rs 14,000,” said an employee at a PG facility in Laxmi Nagar. The lane outside was dug up, forcing students to navigate an uneven stretch.The worry is visible closer to North Campus too. In Mukherjee Nagar, another major hub for students and competitive exam aspirants, electric poles and walls are plastered with boards offering rooms, phone numbers to call and promises of “Hi-Fi” facilities.From the road, it is not always obvious which buildings are being used as PGs. The reality becomes clear only after going upstairs. At one such building, cracked walls, dim staircases, exposed wires and electricity meters greet one at the entrance.“The condition is bad at many PGs, including mine, especially for the rent we pay. It is Rs 10,000-15,000 per person in a double-sharing room. If there is an emergency, it would be very difficult to rescue people,” said Devyani, who lives in Mukherjee Nagar. “But we don’t have many options, given it is closer to the campus.”In Guru Mandi, Vijay Nagar, getting to some PGs is a squeeze in itself. Narrow lanes are packed tight with houses. At one place, a cramped staircase takes you past the landlord’s portion before another flight leads up to the PG rooms. There are no visible fire extinguishers, and barely any ventilation.Students alleged several residential buildings are being used as PGs or for commercial accommodation, raising questions about whether adequate fire safety and other measures are in place.“I pay Rs 16,000 for a room on double sharing. The room is so small. Thankfully, I have a balcony, but not all rooms have that. These are residential buildings but are being run commercially without the necessary permissions. That means safety measures are often missing,” said Sukriti.Amen, who lives in Vijay Nagar, said the condition of some buildings was “frightening”. “When I hit my wall, it feels like it is moving. It is really scary,” he said. For Yashi, the nearby pocket of Malka Ganj is “much worse”.Apart from the lack of basic safety clearances and measures, the narrow lanes raise a bigger worry -- if something goes wrong, how quickly can students get out, and can emergency teams get in?The concern is not hypothetical. In 2023, a fire at a Mukherjee Nagar coaching centre trapped several students, who smashed windows and escaped using ropes, wires and pipes. In April, a transformer fire in Laxmi Nagar spread to a residential building, gutting 14 flats and forcing nearly 50 people to flee. Firefighters struggled to reach the site because of narrow, excavated roads.Across these student hubs, the issue goes beyond rent or room size. articles.title: Hasan Piker rejects Lindsay Clancy ‘support’ claim, says Polymarket may be ‘stress testing’ misinformation about him
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Hasan Piker has rejected Polymarket’s claim that he “comes out in support” of Lindsay Clancy, saying the wording badly misrepresents his position on t.
articles.body: Hasan Piker has rejected Polymarket’s claim that he “comes out in support” of Lindsay Clancy, saying the wording badly misrepresents his position on the case. The political commentator responded on September 7 after Polymarket posted the claim about him. Piker said he was confused by it and suggested the platform was testing how far it could go in misstating his views. His reaction comes after he discussed Clancy’s case and the role of postpartum psychosis, while also rejecting an online theory that her husband, Patrick Clancy, was responsible for the deaths of their children.Hasan Piker reacts to Polymarket’s Lindsay Clancy claimPolymarket posted on September 7: “Hasan Piker comes out in support of Lindsay Clancy.” Piker replied: “this one even confused me im ngl, i guess they’re stress testing how much they can lie about my positions on this website?”He later added: “up next: hasan piker thinks working out is ‘promoting body fascism’.” The second line was clearly a sarcastic example of what he sees as an exaggerated description of his views, rather than a serious statement about his beliefs.The dispute comes from Piker’s recent discussion of the Lindsay Clancy case. Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse from Duxbury, Massachusetts, is accused of killing her three children, Cora, Dawson and Callan, on January 24, 2023. She has not denied strangling the children. Her defense has argued that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible because of her mental state.Piker has focused on that distinction. In his recent coverage, he argued that accepting Clancy committed the killings does not settle the separate legal question of whether she was responsible for her actions at the time.He also criticized the medical system’s handling of her mental health treatment and said the case raised reasonable doubt over first-degree murder. At the same time, he rejected online claims that Patrick Clancy killed the children and framed his wife.Lindsay Clancy mistrial leaves case unresolvedClancy’s trial ended in a mistrial on September 4 after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict. The 12-member jury had deliberated for about seven days and more than 38 hours before the judge ended the case. Reports said the jury was split 11-1, with 11 jurors leaning toward a finding that Clancy was not criminally responsible because of mental illness.The mistrial does not clear Clancy of the charges. She remains under psychiatric care at Tewksbury Hospital, and prosecutors have not yet decided whether to try the case again. A status hearing is scheduled for September 29, when the next legal steps are expected to become clearer.Piker’s response, therefore, was aimed at the description of his position, not a claim that Clancy should simply walk free. His comments have placed him in a wider online argument over postpartum psychosis, criminal responsibility and how the case should be understood.His September 7 posts show that he believes the Polymarket wording turned that argument into a much broader claim than the one he has actually made.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: IShowSpeed and Jasontheween’s heated emotions debate goes viral after bizarre pain claim
articles.summary: US Streamers News: A casual conversation between IShowSpeed and Jasontheween quickly turned into one of the internet’s more unexpected streamer debates. The two creators.
articles.body: A casual conversation between IShowSpeed and Jasontheween quickly turned into one of the internet’s more unexpected streamer debates. The two creators disagreed over what emotions and pain actually are, with Speed taking a highly literal view rooted in neurons, nerve signals and atoms. Jasontheween was far less convinced. Their exchange, filmed during a 72-hour collaboration, soon spread across social media.IShowSpeed and Jasontheween clash over what emotions meanThe debate surfaced in a clip from Jasontheween’s YouTube video, “Living With IShowSpeed For 72 Hours!” The moment came during a conversation involving content creator Marlon, who asked Speed when he had last cried.Speed said he had cried while playing The Walking Dead, then used the question to explain his broader view of human emotions. His explanation quickly became the focus of the clip.“When I was playing this one game... I was playing The Walking Dead. We're humans. Humans have emotions. Yes, you can block out these nerve signals, that's what's called emotions. Emotions are nerve signals that we send to our brain. When we have emotions, there are nerve signals that's getting sent to our brain of these emotions. Then we make these emotions like, 'I'm sad.' Because it... Signals! Nerve signals!”Jasontheween and Marlon laughed at the explanation. Jason then pushed back, questioning Speed’s description of emotions as nerve signals.“Emotions is a nerve signal?! It's not nerve signals! It's not nerve signals! It's not nerve anything! Nerve is like what you feel in the body!”Speed did not back down. Instead, he pointed toward the role of neurons in the brain and insisted that his explanation made sense.“Our brain is full of neurons! What is he talking about?! Nerve signals. Neurons, nerves, same thing! We have nerve signals inside of our brain, Jasontheween!”The exchange was less about reaching an answer than two streamers trying to make sense of a complicated subject in real time. That spontaneity helped give the moment its viral appeal.IShowSpeed sparks another debate over pain and atomsThe conversation became even more unusual when Speed shifted from emotions to physical pain. He argued that what people experience as pain can be understood as signals produced by the body and processed by the brain.“Bro, everything is atoms. Everything in this world is atoms. You're atoms. We don't actually feel pain; that's just atoms. That's just disrupting the... theoretically, we don't feel pain. Pain is just, exactly, like, we see a cut; it's a nerve signal getting sent to our brain like, 'Yo! This needs to get patched up! This part of our body needs to get patched up! Everything is atoms. This is atoms. Everything in this world is atoms.”That claim prompted an immediate response from Jasontheween, who offered a much simpler argument based on his own experience.“We don't feel pain?! I feel pain every day! I feel pain every day!”The disagreement turned an ordinary creator collaboration into a highly shareable moment. Neither streamer appeared interested in delivering a formal scientific explanation. Instead, their contrasting reactions, jokes and increasingly abstract ideas made the conversation entertaining enough to travel well beyond the original video.For viewers, the appeal was simple: Speed approached the subject with absolute confidence, while Jasontheween repeatedly challenged him. The result was an amusing clash over something everyone experiences but few people casually stop to analyze.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Canada released 26 bison into Banff National Park in 2017; the herd grew rapidly as scientists tracked its return to the wild
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 2017, Parks Canada released 16 plains bison into Banff National Park, beginning a carefully monitored effort to restore the animals to a landscape .
articles.body: In 2017, Parks Canada released 16 plains bison into Banff National Park, beginning a carefully monitored effort to restore the animals to a landscape where they had been absent for more than a century. The herd was initially kept in a soft-release pasture before being allowed to roam across a 1,200-square-kilometre reintroduction zone in 2018. What followed was rapid population growth and years of tracking as scientists monitored the bison's health, movements and use of their new mountain habitat. According to a Parks Canada report, the population rose from 16 animals in February 2017 to 26 by the end of that year, 65 by 2021, and about 80 by autumn 2022. The five-year pilot recorded an average annual population growth rate of 33%. GPS and radio-collar monitoring also showed how the herd explored its surroundings, gradually establishing more predictable movement patterns while remaining largely within the designated reintroduction zone.Canada’s bison population grew after 2017Parks Canada's figures show that the plains bison population in Banff National Park grew steadily during the five-year reintroduction pilot. Sixteen animals were translocated to the park in February 2017, with the population reaching 26 by the end of that year. It then increased to 36 in 2018, 39 in 2019, 56 in 2020 and 65 in 2021.By autumn 2022, the population had reached approximately 80 bison. Over the five-year pilot, Parks Canada recorded an average population growth rate of 33% a year, while natural mortality remained below 1% annually. The agency noted that growth was expected to slow as the mainly young founding animals aged and the herd's sex ratio became more balanced.The reintroduction was closely monitored from the beginning. During the initial soft-release period, the bison remained in an enclosed pasture while Parks Canada staff monitored their condition and behaviour. In summer 2018, the animals were released into a 1,200-square-kilometre reintroduction zone, where monitoring continued as the herd explored its new surroundings.Radio collars were used to track the animals, with at least 10% of the population collared. The data showed that the bison explored 257 square kilometres of the reintroduction zone during the pilot, with 81.7% of that exploration in the first year. Their median daily movement was about 1.9 kilometres, while large and rapid movements declined by 51% after the first year.Parks Canada used fences to keep bison from leaving the zoneAs the bison became established in Banff, most remained within the designated reintroduction zone. By autumn 2022, the majority of the approximately 80 animals were also within 30 kilometres of the soft-release pasture where they had spent their first 18 months. Their annual home range contracted from 133.2 square kilometres to 92.9 square kilometres between the first and second years.Only four males dispersed outside the reintroduction zone during the pilot. Two were recaptured and relocated, while two were destroyed under the park's bison excursion response plan. Parks Canada also used drift fences and low-stress herding, known as hazing, to manage movements. Two drift fences prevented movements outside the zone on 50 occasions, while hazing was used seven times.Bison spent more time at higher elevationsThe tracking data showed that the reintroduced bison used parts of Banff's landscape differently from what the original habitat assessment had predicted. Parks Canada found that the animals spent more time at higher elevations, on steeper slopes, in shrubs and farther from water than expected. The bison also repeatedly returned to higher elevations during the peak growing season.Scat analysis indicated that forage at higher elevations was nutritionally superior and more palatable during summer than forage at lower elevations. Health monitoring found that the founder animals generally remained in good to very good body condition, parasite counts were low, and no sick animals were detected. Only two natural bison mortalities were recorded during the pilot, both involving wolf predation of newborn calves in spring 2020 and 2021.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Night entry, lifting clothes don't amount to rape bid: Jharkhand HC
articles.summary: RANCHI: Entering a woman's house at night and trying to lift her clothes may be criminal, but it does not amount to an attempt to rape, Jharkhand HC h.
articles.body: RANCHI: Entering a woman's house at night and trying to lift her clothes may be criminal, but it does not amount to an attempt to rape, Jharkhand HC has ruled while drawing a line between outraging a woman's modesty and attempting to rape her.Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, deciding a criminal appeal on Aug 31, held that acts attributed to the appellant did not cross that legal threshold. HC upheld his conviction for using criminal force against a woman with the intention of outraging her modesty, finding evidence sufficient for the lesser offence. The judgement was released Monday.The court modified a July 25 sessions court order from East Singhbhum district that had sentenced the man to four years of rigorous imprisonment for attempted rape. It reduced his sentence to the nearly eight months he had already spent in custody, saying that was sufficient to meet the ends of justice. The appeal was partly allowed.The case dates to the night of Dec 26, 1999. The man was arrested on Dec 27 and later a chargesheet was filed alleging attempted rape.The trial court convicted him of attempted rape and handed him a four-year prison term. The appellant approached the high court.Justice Srivastava said an act can amount to attempted rape only when it is sufficiently proximate to the commission of rape. The evidence in this case did not make the leap from criminal force intended to outrage a woman's modesty to an attempt to rape, HC ruled.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Germany turned apartment balconies into tiny solar power plants; more than 550,000 systems are now helping renters generate their own electricity
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Across Germany, solar power is showing up in an unlikely place: apartment balconies. Small panels are being fixed to railings and walls, giving renter.
articles.body: Across Germany, solar power is showing up in an unlikely place: apartment balconies. Small panels are being fixed to railings and walls, giving renters a way to generate some of their own electricity without owning a house or installing a rooftop system. Known as Balkonkraftwerk, or “balcony power plant”, these compact setups can be bought for around 500 euros and connected to an apartment through a plug-in microinverter. What began as a niche idea has grown rapidly, with more than 550,000 systems recorded across the country by 2024.Changes to technical rules, simpler registration and new protections for tenants helped remove some of the barriers that had kept the technology from spreading. The systems are not large enough to transform Germany’s energy supply, and their financial savings vary with sunlight and orientation. But on a household level, they offer renters a practical way to produce a little electricity themselves.Germany turned balconies into mini solar power stationsThe German term Balkonkraftwerk roughly translates as “balcony power plant”. The name sounds grander than the equipment itself.A typical setup consists of one or two solar panels attached to a balcony railing or wall, along with a microinverter. The panels generate direct-current electricity, the inverter converts it for household use, and the system sends the power into the home's electrical circuit.For someone living in a detached house, rooftop solar is the obvious route. Apartment residents have a different problem. They may have plenty of sunlight reaching their balcony but no control over the roof above them.That distinction helps explain why balcony systems found an audience in Germany. They offered renters a way around one of the biggest barriers to household solar: ownership of the building.According to Grist (an American non-profit online magazine), the hardware was also relatively inexpensive. Around 500 euros, or roughly $550 at the time, could buy a basic system. Installation was far less involved than fitting a conventional rooftop array, making it something closer to a household appliance than a major building project.The 2019 rules opened the door for plug-in balcony solarBalcony solar had existed for years before it became a mainstream product. The turning point came when Germany began changing the rules around small plug-in photovoltaic systems.Technical regulations introduced in 2019 allowed these devices to use standard electrical plugs and supply electricity to the household grid. That gave manufacturers and campaigners a clearer framework in which to sell and promote them.The growth was gradual at first. Then several things happened at once.During the pandemic, people were spending much more time at home, and small DIY projects became common. Rising electricity prices following Russia's invasion of Ukraine added another reason to look for ways of reducing household energy costs.The result was a rapid rise in installations. About half of the more than 550,000 systems recorded by 2024 had been installed during 2023 alone. In the first six months of 2024, balcony photovoltaic capacity added up to about 200 megawatts.Simpler rules and subsidies opened balcony solar to more rentersThe equipment itself was only part of the story. Germany also began removing some of the administrative obstacles surrounding balcony solar.In April 2024, the federal government simplified registration and permitting requirements. A few months later, lawmakers approved changes giving renters greater protection against landlords simply refusing a balcony solar installation.That matters in a country where more than half of the population lives in rented accommodation. A rooftop system can involve questions of ownership, building structure and access. A small panel attached to a balcony creates a different set of issues, but landlords can still object to alterations to their buildings.Some German cities have gone further by offering financial assistance. Berlin, Kiel and other local authorities have provided subsidies designed to encourage residents to install small photovoltaic systems.The policy approach has therefore worked on several fronts: make the equipment relatively simple, reduce paperwork, protect tenants and, in some places, help cover the purchase price.An 800-watt limit keeps balcony solar small but usefulIt would be easy to assume that hundreds of thousands of balcony systems must be making a major contribution to Germany's electricity supply. They are not.The individual systems are simply too small. German regulations at the time limited balcony solar installations to 800 watts. That is enough to run or offset part of the electricity demand from small household appliances, but it is nowhere near the output of a conventional rooftop array.For individual households, the savings can still be worthwhile. Matthias Weyland, who has two panels on his apartment balcony, paid around $530 for a system rated at 600 watts. He estimated that it would reduce his annual electricity costs by roughly $100, giving him a payback period of about five years.A south-facing balcony with little shade can generate considerably more useful electricity than a shaded installation facing in an unfavourable direction. The number of panels, the position of the balcony and local weather all affect the result.Peter Stratmann of Germany's Federal Network Agency estimated that a relatively large, well-positioned balcony system in a sunny south-facing location could supply around 15 percent of a household's electricity.The panels bring electricity generation into view at homeThere is another effect that is harder to measure on a national energy chart. Balcony solar makes electricity visible.For most households, electricity arrives invisibly through a socket. A person switches on a washing machine and rarely thinks about whether the power being used was generated by a coal plant, a wind turbine or a solar panel hundreds of kilometres away.A balcony array changes that relationship. On a bright afternoon, the panels are producing power right outside the apartment.Because the systems generally do not include batteries, the timing matters. Electricity generated during the day is most useful when it is consumed at roughly the same time. That can encourage owners to run appliances when their panels are producing.Some systems come with apps showing how much electricity has been generated. Owners can watch the output rise and fall with the weather, and compare their production from one day to another.For some households, that has turned into a small daily ritual. The amount generated becomes something to check, share and compare.It also makes energy consumption less abstract. A washing machine running in bright sunshine has a visible connection to the panels outside.Why Germany has embraced balcony solar so stronglyThe technology is not exclusive to Germany. Balcony systems have become increasingly visible in countries including Austria, France and the Netherlands.Germany, however, has developed an unusually large market for them.Part of that comes down to housing. A large share of the population lives in apartments, meaning there is a substantial group of people who may want solar power but cannot simply install panels on a roof.There is also the country's longer-running push towards renewable energy. Small photovoltaic systems fit neatly into that effort because they allow households to participate without waiting for a major building project.The emotional appeal is surprisingly straightforward, too. The panels provide something people can see and control.A household may not be able to influence the national electricity mix, but it can put two panels on a balcony and watch them generate electricity.That is a modest form of energy independence rather than anything approaching off-grid living.Solar panels sparked disputes over safety, appearance and landlord approvalSome landlords and property managers have raised concerns about the appearance of panels on apartment buildings, while others have questioned electrical safety or demanded additional inspections before allowing installations.Weyland encountered that problem himself. His property management company imposed requirements he considered unreasonable, including a formal inspection of the building's electrical system.The dispute ended up in court. In October 2023, a German court ruled in his favour, allowing the balcony system to be installed.Disagreements between tenants and landlords over balcony solar continued to appear even as the federal government moved to make installations easier. The legal changes introduced in 2024 were intended to give renters a stronger position, reducing the ability of landlords to block systems without good reason.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: TANGERANG, Indonesia, Sept 8 (Reuters) - Indonesia has reopened its main airport in Jakarta and four others that had been closed due to volcanic ash from a s...
articles.body:

TANGERANG, Indonesia, Sept 8 (Reuters) - Indonesia has reopened its main airport in Jakarta and four others that had been closed due to volcanic ash from a series of eruptions ‌at Mount Anak Krakatau, transport minister Dudy Purwagandhi said in a statement on Tuesday.

Ash from ‌Anak Krakatau, which sits halfway between Java and Sumatra islands, has blanketed Jakarta and some surrounding areas since its initial ​eruption late on Friday. It led to the closure of eight airports for safety reasons, with more than 340,000 travellers impacted.

Dudy said the Soekarno-Hatta Airport, Jakarta's main airport, resumed operations on Tuesday after wind blew the ash away from the vicinity.

Four other airports, including a smaller one in Jakarta and another ‌in the neighbouring city of Bandung, ⁠also reopened on Tuesday.

Another airport had already reopened on Monday, while two remain closed.

Alvin Pratama Putra, 31, who arrived at the Soekarno-Hatta on Sunday to ⁠travel to South Korea for work, said his cancelled flight had now been rescheduled to Thursday.

"What can you do? It's the nature. It's dangerous for the plane if you force it," he said, adding that ​he ​had been sleeping on a bench at the airport.

Dudy ​said authorities still needed to check ‌on the airworthiness of the 178 planes that were at Soekarno-Hatta during the closure.

"Perhaps it'll take some little extra time to prepare the planes," he said.

Around 341,000 people have been affected by the delay, diversion, or cancellation of 2,961 flights across all the shuttered airports, Chief Infrastructure Minister Agus Harimurti Yudhoyono said on Monday.

Anak Krakatau erupted again three times on Tuesday morning, the volcano monitoring ‌agency said. The severity of these eruptions was not ​immediately known. Anak Krakatau remains at level 3 in the ​four-tiered alert system.

The volcano is one ​of about 130 active volcanoes in Indonesia, which straddles the "Pacific Ring of Fire", ‌a highly seismically active zone where different ​plates on the Earth's ​crust meet to create a large number of earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

Anak Krakatau, which means child of Krakatau, began emerging a century ago from the area previously occupied by ​Krakatau, then known as Krakatoa. The ‌older volcano destroyed itself in mass eruptions in 1883, which killed more than 36,000 ​people after triggering a series of tsunamis.

(Reporting by Stanley Widianto and Yuddy Cahya ​Budiman; Editing by Christopher Cushing and John Mair)

articles.title: Gifted Manipuri guitarist who built his life around music in Delhi for 20 years beaten to death outside home
articles.summary: NEW DELHI/KOLKATA: Chongtham Vikram Singh was a gifted guitarist who had spent years turning music into his language, playing lead guitar for bands in.
articles.body: NEW DELHI/KOLKATA: Chongtham Vikram Singh was a gifted guitarist who had spent years turning music into his language, playing lead guitar for bands in Manipur before moving to Delhi nearly 20 years ago and building a life around his passion. On Sunday night, his music fell silent after he was allegedly beaten mercilessly by eight people outside his home. He died during treatment around 6.30am Monday.The men were allegedly intoxicated and creating a ruckus outside the house around 11pm. According to Singh's family, he went downstairs to stop them. A few minutes later, Singh (55) was heard banging on the door and screaming, "Thong hango! Thong hango! (open the door, open the door)."His son, 20-year-old Yaiphaba, found Singh in a semi-conscious state, with his T-shirt ripped apart. He was rushed to Holy Family Hospital, where doctors found that his blood pressure had fallen below 50mm Hg. His condition was too critical for surgery and he died Monday morning.A resident of Thangmeiband Lourung Purel Leikai in Imphal West, Singh opened a music school in Delhi, mentored students at home and also taught at Delhi School of Music. His musical journey took him to the Rock'n'Roots project, where he collaborated with Rajasthani folk singer Mame Khan. He also collaborated with other renowned musicians for cultural shows and concerts.Singh, a cousin of Lakshmipriya Devi, the director of India's first BAFTA Award-winning film, Boong, is survived by his wife Jyotsana (54) and son Yaiphaba. While Jyotsana works as a senior consultant with an MNC, Yaiphaba is a law student. Singh's mother, 86-year-old Chongtham Ongbi Kamala Devi, is a renowned classical and modern Manipuri singer.Talking to TOI from Imphal, Singh's brother, Vivek, said, "We haven't told our father, Dr Chongtham Birendra Singh, who is 96, about it, fearing that he might not be able to bear the loss. My mother is unconsolable."Friends remembered Singh as a gentle and accomplished musician who was passionate about his craft.Manipuri associations in Delhi said though the postmortem was over, they didn't want the body to be sent back to Manipur till justice was done. "Once the last rites are over, only the family bears the loss, and the incident fades into oblivion," a Manipuri activist in Delhi said. articles.title: India's carbon credit scheme gets UK recognition under its carbon tax mechanism
articles.summary: UK News: The United Kingdom has formally recognised India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) under its indicative list of overseas carbon pricing mechanisms.
articles.body: The United Kingdom has formally recognised India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) under its indicative list of overseas carbon pricing mechanisms that could qualify for relief under the UK’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).India’s CCTS has been included in the UK’s published indicative list of overseas carbon pricing schemes, communicated by HM Treasury to India’s Bureau of Energy Efficiency, ANI reported, quoting Commerce Ministry officials.The scheme was found to meet the eligibility requirements under Part 3, Regulation 6 of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (Calculation of CBAM Rate and Determination of Carbon Price Relief) Regulations 2026.How will Indian exporters benefit?Under the recognition, UK importers of eligible Indian goods covered by CBAM can claim relief for the carbon price already paid on those goods under India’s CCTS. The relief will be subject to evidence and verification requirements under UK law."This will reduce the effective CBAM liability on Indian goods, directly benefiting Indian exporters to the UK," an official told PTI.The amount of relief will depend on the effective carbon price paid on the goods in India. The move could help prevent carbon costs from being imposed twice on the same goods — once in India and again under the UK’s CBAM.What is India's CCTS?India notified the CCTS as a market-based mechanism to reduce, remove or avoid greenhouse gas emissions by putting a price on emissions through the trading of Carbon Credit Certificates.The scheme is being implemented by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and funded through fees and charges collected from entities covered by it, along with the bureau’s own resources.The UK’s recognition follows technical discussions between the commerce ministry and its UK counterpart on the design and implementation of the CCTS. According to ministry sources, the decision is consistent with the UK CBAM’s principle of avoiding double taxation on goods that have already been subject to an eligible carbon price in their country of origin.The UK decided in December 2023 to introduce its CBAM from 2027. The mechanism will impose a carbon-related charge on imports of certain emissions-intensive products, including iron and steel, aluminium, fertiliser, hydrogen, ceramics, glass and cement.Indian exporters of these products could face higher costs once the mechanism takes effect. Recognition of the CCTS could help offset part of that liability where the carbon price paid in India qualifies for relief.India and the UK will continue cooperation on carbon-market design and implementation through the UK-India Energy Memorandum of Understanding and the Partnership for Market Implementation. The two countries will also maintain dialogue on carbon pricing and the interaction between India’s CCTS and UK CBAM rules.The recognition comes after India and the UK implemented their comprehensive economic and trade partnership on July 15. Merchandise trade between the two countries stood at $25.1 billion in 2025-26, while bilateral services trade was $35.4 billion in 2024.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Schools facing acute teacher shortage in core subjects: TISS
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Schools surveyed across 10 states - Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Punjab, Odisha and Mizoram -.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Schools surveyed across 10 states - Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Punjab, Odisha and Mizoram - report acute teacher shortages in fundamental subjects such as mathematics and science (35%), English (31%), and in regional languages (30%). Moreover, it was found that only 51% of mathematics teachers studied the subject at under-graduate level, highlighting credential mismatches.Govt schools face recruitment delays and staff shortages (33% reported staffing challenges), but little retention difficulty. Private schools, on the other hand, recruit faster but face higher teacher attrition (as reported by 14%), especially in rural areas (18%).These are some of the findings from the executive summary of the biennial report on the 'State of Teachers, Teaching and Teacher Education for India' (SoTTTER) 2025 by TISS Centre of Excellence in Teacher Education (CETE) released on Teachers' Day. The SoTTTER 2025 focuses on three landmark policies that reached key implementation milestones in 2025 - 15 years of the Right To Education Act (2009), 10 years of the Rights of People with Disabilities Act (2016), and five years of the National Education Policy (2020).Comparing the data from the SoTTTER 2023, the report highlighted a critical aspect of the student enrollment falling sharply by 1.55 crore in five years - from 26.5 crores in 2021-22 to 23.2 crores in 2024-25. At the same time, the teaching workforce grew by six lakh, thereby improving the average student-teacher ratio. The report also highlighted 'an accelerated privatisation and feminisation of the teaching force'. Women now make up 54% of the teaching workforce, up from 51% in the previous report. However, a clear urban-rural gap remains - women comprise 67% of urban teachers, while rural schools remain male-dominated, with women accounting for only 47%.The summary of SoTTTER 2025 also underscores a worrying rise in multi-grade classrooms in govt schools, where a single teacher instructs students from multiple grades. In 2025, nearly half of govt primary schools operated as multi-grade classrooms, up from 38% recorded in 2023.The report, which reviewed the structural and pedagogical shifts in the Indian teaching workforce, will be officially released in Oct this year, in collaboration with the Language and Learning Foundation.Prof Padma M Sarangapani, former chairperson of CETE, currently Dean of IMSE, Mahindra University, and principal investigator of the study, noted that while many aspiring teachers are genuinely motivated to enter the profession, the lack of job security and employment opportunities acts as a disincentive. Nearly half of the teachers surveyed also felt that the profession is misunderstood and that their work is not sufficiently valued or appreciated. "Another major concern is the delayed recruitment process, which can sometimes take seven to eight years. With no guarantee of securing a job, this uncertainty can significantly demotivate young aspirants," she said. The report also gives recommendations for resolving the persistent teacher shortages.Apart from the national datasets from the U-DISE+ 2024-25 and Periodic Labour Force Survey 2024-25, the report used primary data from the field survey covering 499 schools in the 10 states. Some of the positive developments include improved working conditions for teachers, reduction in single-teacher schools, and increase in the numbers of teachers with greater local connect.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news.
